pain.title: Hiring a junior is a bet. I make it a safe one.
pain.subtitle: I've shipped to production in two public institutions and one product company. I measure what I build and I care about the why behind the architecture: auth, access control, data models, tests.
pain.q1: Will they need months of hand-holding?
pain.q2: Will their code survive code review?
pain.q3: Do they understand auth, permissions and data, or just UI?
pain.q4: Can they ship, or only finish tutorials?
pain.closing: Fast delivery, without code that hurts later.
pain.worry: What teams worry about when hiring a junior
pain.q5: Will they communicate clearly with an international team?

objections.title: Straight answers
objections.a1: True, and that’s why I show numbers instead of adjectives. In under two years I’ve shipped in three organizations, and one project cut LCP by 75%.
objections.a2: They’re real users, real deployments and real maintenance. I run deployment and evolutionary maintenance in production, with 50+ routes and RBAC.
objections.q3: “Can you work with an international team?”
objections.a3: English C1, now advancing to C2, and comfortable with remote work.
objections.a4: No. Fastify and Node back-ends, PostgreSQL with Prisma/Drizzle, and AWS Lambda pipelines are all on my GitHub.
